2026-12-22.title: Fourth Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: The Son of God born of a woman
The one who came to witness to the Light
2026-12-22.verse: But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
theo: Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed: “When the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman.” The eternal Son receives a human mother; and through him we receive adoption, so that the Spirit in our hearts cries “Abba! Father!” We are no longer slaves but children and heirs.

John's Prologue continues: John the Baptist “came as a witness to testify to the light.” The true light came to his own, “and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him… he gave power to become children of God.” Christmas is a choice: to receive or to refuse.
outline: Ask: what does it mean to you to call God “Abba, Father”?
God chose the moment; the Son was born of a woman.
Through Christ we are adopted children and heirs.
His own did not receive him; will we?
“To all who received him, he gave power to become children of God.”
live: Pray the Our Father slowly, savouring the word “Father”.
Make one concrete space in your Christmas for Christ: confession, prayer, the poor.
2026-12-22.prayer: Father, in the fullness of time you sent your Son, born of a woman, to make us your children. Let me receive him and live as your child. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we cry with the Spirit, Abba, Father, in the Our Father. Receiving the Son, we become children of God.

quick: In the fullness of time God sent his Son, born of a woman.
Through him we are children and heirs.
Christmas is a choice: to receive him.
2026-12-22.action: Make one concrete space for Christ this Christmas.
2026-12-22.question: Have I truly received Christ, or only celebrated around him?

family.explain: Some people did not welcome Jesus. But to those who welcome him, he gives the gift of becoming God's children.
family.intention: We pray that our family may make room for Jesus this Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make room for Jesus, and for someone in need, at Christmas?”

pm.open: Abba, Father, in the fullness of time you sent your Son, born of a woman. As we gather, pour the Spirit of your Son into our hearts and make us your children. Amen.
share: God sent his Son born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). What does it mean to me that God became a real child?
His own people did not accept him (John 1:11). Where in my life is there ‘no room’ for him?
How will I receive him this Christmas?
pm.resp: Abba, Father, we are your children.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome Christ and make room for the poor.
For expectant mothers this Christmas, that they may be safe and joyful.
For those who reject Christ, that they may come to receive him.
For migrants, strangers and the homeless, that they may find welcome.
For our families, that we may live as children of God.
pm.close: Father, through your Son born of Mary you have made us your children. Make room in our hearts for him, and let us welcome him in every stranger this Christmas. Amen.

illus: A family in Thodupuzha decided to leave one place empty at their Christmas table, with a lit candle, for “the stranger Jesus”. That year they invited a lonely migrant worker from Odisha who lived nearby. Their children still remember it as their best Christmas.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Galatians: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children (Galatians 4:4–5).

Born of a woman. God did not drop from the sky as an adult. He chose a mother, a womb, a birth, a childhood. He entered our history at a particular time and place: in the days of Caesar Augustus, in Bethlehem of Judea. The fullness of time was the moment God chose.

And the purpose: so that we might receive adoption as children. Because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba! Father! (Galatians 4:6). The Son became a son of Mary so that we might become sons and daughters of God.

In the Gospel John introduces John the Baptist: there was a man sent from God, whose name was John. He came as a witness to testify to the light. He himself was not the light (John 1:6–8). Then the sad line: he came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him (John 1:11).
But the Gospel continues: to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God (John 1:12). Christmas is a question addressed to each of us: will I receive him?

Every family in Kerala is busy preparing: stars, cribs, cakes, new clothes. Good. But let us not be like Bethlehem, which had no room. Let us make room: a quiet hour of prayer, a good confession, reconciliation with someone. Then, receiving him, we will become what he came to make us: children of God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus came so that we could be God's children. When you pray Our Father, remember that God is your Father!

intro: The Son born of a woman makes us God's children; to receive him is to become one.

sub: The Son takes flesh from Mary.
God enters history at the chosen time.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.
points.apply: Thank Mary for giving Jesus to the world.

q: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
And because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba! Father!” So you are no longer a slave but a child, and if a child then also an heir, through God.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly today.

sub: His own did not accept him.
Those who receive him become God's children.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God.
points.apply: Make room for Christ through confession.

concl: The Son became a child of Mary so that we might become children of God.
2026-12-22.resolve: Prepare a place for Jesus: confession before Christmas.
